calls.thesis: Reiterated BUY / bullish, thesis unchanged: a report that OpenAI plans to buy Google AI chips is being read as bearish for Nvidia, but he says he is not afraid for Nvidia — OpenAI needs multiple compute sources and cannot let one player dictate supply, the market is compute-starved, and it does not change much for Nvidia; Nvidia is also expanding its Meta Vera Rubin work, is already live at Oracle with Vera Rubin NVL72 / Vera CPU, and he lists Nvidia among the big winners, concluding his bullish AI thesis is still in place even if prices keep falling.
calls.price_at_call: No price stated; $3bn Nvidia investment in Meta as captioned

calls.thesis: Reiterated BUY / bullish: Nvidia fell ~4% on 22 Oct in the AI sell-off but he says demand is not slowing and his bullish thesis is getting stronger, not smaller. Nvidia's DSX pods (pre-built Vera Rubin AI factories) cut on-site deployment from ~6 months to as little as 14 days, shortening the period where capital earns no revenue and reducing lender risk; its third-party financing platform (Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, KKR) targets mobilising over $500bn of capital over time, and revenue commitments/backstops support selected capacity. He stresses Nvidia is not itself lending $500bn.
calls.price_at_call: No share price stated; Nvidia down ~4% on 22 Oct as stated

calls.thesis: Very, very bullish reiterated: the new DSX pods (captions render them 'DSX') — pre-built shipping-container AI factories with Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, power and cooling built in — cut AI-factory production from ~6 months to as little as 14 days, removing execution and lender risk and making Nvidia the only supplier doing this right now; he calls it a massive win that lets Nvidia scale and sell more. Other GTC Berlin items (agent safety, robotics, Vera vs Blackwell) were mostly repeats for channel followers.
calls.price_at_call: Up ~2.5% on the day, down ~1.2% after hours; no share price stated

calls.thesis: Remains bullish and calm on Nvidia and the AI industry: SpaceXAI/xAI (captions render it 'SpaceX') is scaling compute fast (1.7 GW active end-Sep, ~2 GW end-Oct, 2.5 GW by year-end, ~13 GW targeted by end of next year, ~200,000 GB300s coming online per month), Super Micro raised its guide sharply on server demand, and new compute deployments are reportedly paying back in under a year — he reads all of it as proof AI GPU demand is still extreme.
calls.price_at_call: No share price stated; Nvidia up about 2% on the day in the video's market roundup

Reiterated BUY: Microsoft building its own Maia inference chip is NOT bearish for Nvidia — compute demand is so large it does not dent Nvidia demand, and Nvidia remains best on total cost of ownership.
